Robbyant releases LingBot-Touch for shared tactile representations

The model uses nearly 5,000 hours of data and reports results on 26 tasks; a new hand still needs action-policy training.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗10 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

A shared representation of touch

Ant Group’s Robbyant has released LingBot-Touch to learn shared tactile representations for robots. Magnetic, visuotactile and piezoresistive sensors produce different data formats. Modality-specific tokenizers and a Haptic Transformer let the system learn common contact patterns.

Training and evaluation evidence

The project reports 4,983 hours of pretraining data from gloves and robot hands, and evaluates 26 tasks on SharpaWave and XHand6 hands. Its experiments report success gains of 14–26 percentage points over versions without tactile input. These are developer-reported results, not certification across all operating conditions.

Transfer still involves training

The tactile encoder can remain frozen while an action policy is trained with demonstrations from a new hand. Transferring the touch representation therefore differs from deploying a new robot without training. Code, a report and models are released for inspection, supporting manipulation research where vision alone is insufficient.
